title: Cost
user: I need the useful work without a premium extension.
engineering: Local collection, statistics and every export must remain independent of a paid model.
decision: Kept the full local path free; the API is an explicitly optional paid boundary.

title: Brand and visual identity
user: The old generic appearance does not feel like my app.
engineering: A strong identity should not need a framework, remote font or stock illustration.
decision: HKS_67 now has a four-color geometric SVG/PNG identity and a restrained hard-border interface.

title: Landscape readability
user: I want aligned controls, not a tall pile of tiny buttons.
engineering: A Chrome popup has a limited width/height; readable text may require vertical scrolling.
decision: Used a 780px landscape shell, compact grouped controls and a wider workspace. No promise of zero vertical scrolling.

title: Narrow layouts and zoom
user: It should work on my laptop, even with less space.
engineering: CSS layout checks cannot certify every OS zoom, browser policy or screen reader.
decision: Verified 320/640/780/1280px document boundaries; disclose that these are not all-device/actual-zoom certification.

title: One Export dropdown
user: Too many format buttons make the screen busy.
engineering: The dropdown must still work without a pointer and expose its open state.
decision: Single collapsed menu with arrow/Home/End navigation, Escape close, focus return and accessible labels.

title: CSV row mess
user: Long URL dumps and multiline cells are hard to scan.
engineering: CSV cannot store column widths, colors, pictures or a different hidden hyperlink target.
decision: Clean uppercase CSV flattens body whitespace and moves media URLs to Media CSV; original text remains in Detailed CSV/JSON.

title: Username/profile separation
user: I want the username and profile link in different columns.
engineering: Presentation labels must not destroy the actual URL or author data.
decision: Separate USERNAME and PROFILE URL; Excel displays a short OPEN PROFILE link while preserving the target.

title: Long numeric IDs
user: Do not corrupt comment identifiers in Excel.
engineering: Quoted CSV alone cannot stop spreadsheet auto-inference or rounding of 19-digit IDs.
decision: Workbook IDs are text; CSV documentation instructs text import. No formula-based ID workaround.

title: Professional Excel
user: A renamed CSV is not a real Excel deliverable.
engineering: OOXML needs valid relationships, styles, tables and charts, not only a .xlsx suffix.
decision: Four real worksheets, two native charts, genuine tables, frozen headers, wrapping and color.
evidence: ZIP/CRC tests; independent openpyxl chart/table parsing

title: Oversized spreadsheet cells
user: I still need all the comment content.
engineering: Excel has a hard 32,767 UTF-16-unit cell limit, and fixed-height rows cannot show everything at once.
decision: Count/label truncation in Coverage; keep JSON lossless and allow the full body through Excel cell/formula-bar inspection.

title: See available media
user: A link is not enough when the image could be displayed.
engineering: The server may reject a URL, omit it, or return a format the browser cannot decode.
decision: Inline image/video previews try returned variants, expose errors and offer explicit retry; no autoplay.

title: Missing photos
user: Can you repair all 80 missing pictures?
engineering: No client can recreate a photo URL that the session never returned without inventing evidence.
decision: Preserved all 80 unavailable-photo labels. Did not substitute synthetic pictures or claim recovery.
evidence: Historical archive; media/core tests; sample report

title: Photos inside Excel
user: I want images beside the corresponding row.
engineering: Fetching everything can leak requests, hit expiry, inflate files and stall small devices.
decision: Opt-in known-CDN downloads: 20 rows, 2 MB/response, 8-second fetch budget/row; PNG stills only. One real returned GIF still is in the sample.
evidence: thumbnails.js; Chrome GIF-to-PNG test; openpyxl image check

title: Top-three definitions
user: Top three likes/comments should be immediately understandable.
engineering: Most-liked comments and most-active commenters are different statistics; filtered data changes both.
decision: Separate top-three liked comments, commenters by collected rows, and threads by collected replies; label denominator and ties.

title: Charts versus invented insight
user: I want useful analysis, not decoration or fabricated conclusions.
engineering: Local counts do not establish sentiment, intent, demographics or causal explanations.
decision: Added content, likes, UTC-time and media charts with methodology; semantic interpretation exists only in the labelled optional AI section.
evidence: Local HTML report; no external analysis requests

title: Partial coverage
user: The platform reports 639; do not quietly call 624 complete.
engineering: Reported counters and returned records can differ for reasons a client cannot conclusively identify.
decision: Display partial status, 624 saved/639 reported, the difference and reply gaps; preserve original source status on import.
evidence: State tests; real archive; imported partial badge

title: Ask ChatGPT automation
user: I want the whole dataset passed to ChatGPT without tedious work.
engineering: Blind website injection/submission is brittle, privacy-sensitive and account/UI dependent.
decision: Preview the complete prompt; copy/open or download it; user pastes/reviews/sends. No claim of automatic website submission.
evidence: AI-dialog fixture; full prompt download check

title: Optional API convenience
user: I would rather generate and download the report directly.
engineering: A model request can cost money and fail on account access, quota, model or context size.
decision: Explicit consent and optional host permission, fixed Responses endpoint, editable model, size/output/time limits and no automatic paid retry.
evidence: Mock provider boundary tests; actual paid account NOT verified

title: API-key handling
user: Do not put my key in a file or saved extension state.
engineering: A browser-memory string is transient, not a hardware vault, and cancellation cannot guarantee no provider charge.
decision: Key is never persisted/exported; clear on request/close/Escape/pagehide; cancellation is best effort.
evidence: Chrome storage and Escape-clearing test; ai.js/ui.js

title: Privacy and anonymization
user: I want an option not to send names.
engineering: Bodies, mentions and context may identify people even after usernames are removed.
decision: Username omission is available; raw objects/profile/signed URLs are excluded from the AI pack; wording explicitly says not anonymization.

title: Untrusted comments and AI output
user: Comments or model output must not run code or hijack the report.
engineering: Source text can contain HTML and prompt-injection attempts; a model may still produce wrong interpretations.
decision: Text nodes/escaping, no executable model HTML, explicit untrusted-data instruction, separately labelled interpretation and evidence.
evidence: HTML script-injection tests; mocked provider-output escaping

title: Resume and live errors
user: A refresh or second tab must not lose hours of collection.
engineering: Concurrent writers, quota exhaustion and rate limits require fail-closed behavior, not heroic promises.
decision: Retained single-writer lease, per-page checkpoints, headload cursors, pause/resume, quota warning and stop-on-critical-error handling.

title: Accessibility and corrections
user: Small print, invisible focus and clipped text are frustrating.
engineering: A successful automated audit is narrower than real assistive-technology testing.
decision: Increased density fonts, native focus/dialog/menu, full-text disclosure, offline Tamil glyph fallback and reduced-motion rule; fixed the selected-tab hover contrast issue found by axe.
evidence: Zero axe violations in setup/review/dialog; manual SR testing NOT verified

title: Maintainability and release claims
user: I need something that can be updated, not an untested bundle.
engineering: Instagram schemas and third-party services change; packaging cannot guarantee every laptop or future version.
decision: Separated analysis/Excel/media/AI modules, formatted readable source, schema/architecture docs and reproducible fixtures. Treat live source/API changes as maintenance work.
evidence: 85 grouped checks plus UI audits; historical 624-row validation; README boundaries
